title: Jagged Molten Japanese Pork Katsudon
description: A spicy and molten Japanese dish featuring cranberry juice and dairy-free friendly ingredients, perfect for a hangover cure. This katsudon recipe combines the crispy texture of pork cutlet with a sweet and spicy sauce.
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Dredge the pork cutlet in the flour, shaking off excess.
Add the pork cutlet to the skillet and cook until browned and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Transfer the pork cutlet to a plate and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the cranberry juice, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and Gochujang.
Bring the sauce to a boil and cook until reduced by half, stirring occasionally.
Add the puff pastry to the skillet, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
Continue cooking the pastry until it is golden brown and crispy.
To assemble the katsudon, place a scoop of steamed rice in a bowl, followed by a piece of the pork cutlet, and finally the molten sauce and pastry.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve immediately.
